item.problem_title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
item.problem_statement: A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size far below the nominal count. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are the quantities decision makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance, and no convention requires the effective size to appear beside it.

item.problem_title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
item.problem_statement: Hazard ratios, odds ratios and model coefficients are routinely presented without naming the intervention, the population, the time horizon or the strategy for each intercurrent event. ICH E9(R1) and the TARGET statement both require that objectives, estimands and sensitivity analyses be aligned, and applied reporting has not caught up. A correctly executed clone-censor-weight analysis with a grace period estimates a marginal contrast between prespecified strategies in the baseline eligible population, and where the artificial censoring enforces adherence that contrast is per-protocol. A bare hazard ratio discloses none of this: not the intervention, not the strategies, not the population, not the horizon, not the handling of intercurrent events. item.problem_title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
item.problem_statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software

item.problem_title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
item.problem_statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Discretizing that onto a grid can reverse the temporal ordering of a treatment and an outcome falling in the same interval, merge several events into one, and define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. Identification and efficient estimation for dynamic interventions in continuous time under counting-process filtrations and irregular monitoring have been established. They do not yet settle the case an emulation on routine data actually faces: a visit process that depends on treatment, combined with effects that occur inside an interval. item.problem_title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
item.problem_statement: Causal forests and meta-learners estimate heterogeneous treatment effects and inherit every identification assumption of the base analysis without relaxing any of them. A subgroup analysis therefore requires subgroup-specific assessment of exchangeability, measurement validity, positivity and uncertainty, and apparent heterogeneity can reflect differential measurement or differential access rather than differential biology. Two further requirements are routinely skipped. Adaptively chosen subgroups need selection-aware inference, because the reported interval otherwise conditions on a subgroup the data chose. And restricting to regions with adequate overlap changes the target population rather than fixing the estimate, so it has to be reported as a change of question. item.problem_title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
item.problem_statement: Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations default to cause-specific hazards or to censoring at the competing event. Censoring does not select among those estimands: it alters the observed-data analysis, and it corresponds to a hypothetical elimination of the competing event only when that intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold, which is a claim the analysis has to make and defend.
